title: From an Em shape to separate notes
summary: See the E minor chord, then practice its notes one at a time.
goal: Learn the open Em shape and play its ascending and descending arpeggio as separate clean notes.
body:
Before starting: complete the open-string and first-fret lessons, and practice steady quarter notes. Tune to Standard, A4 = 440 Hz.

Em means E minor. Its pitch names are E, G, B. The open shape, strings 6 → 1, uses frets 0–2–2–0–0–0 and sounds E2, B2, E3, G3, B3, E4. Suggested fingers are middle finger on string 5 fret 2 and ring finger on string 4 fret 2. The remaining strings are open.

A chord can sound several notes together; an arpeggio plays its notes in sequence. Select the shape to see all its positions or listen to the example. The chord example is for listening and visualization only. This practice does not grade a simultaneous chord.

For the scored arpeggio, stop each previous string before plucking the next one. You may keep the fretting shape while gently damping with your plucking hand, but avoid overlapping notes. Start at 60 BPM; 40–50 BPM gives more time for damping and string changes. After a comfortable repeat, try 70 BPM. If the result reports uncertain signal, check for overlapping strings and input quality before drawing conclusions about the notes.

shape.title: 1. Explore the Em shape
shape.body: Only strings 5 and 4 are fretted, both at fret 2. All six strings belong to the shape. The finger numbers are a suggested fingering; they are not measured from audio.

low-notes.title: 2. Play the low four notes
low-notes.body: Bar 1: strings 6, 5, 4, 3 give E2, B2, E3, G3. Pluck one note per click and stop the previous one.

top-and-turn.title: 3. Reach E4 and turn back
top-and-turn.body: Bar 2: strings 2, 1, 2, 3 give B3, E4, B3, G3. The top E4 is played once.

return-and-rest.title: 4. Return to E2 and rest
return-and-rest.body: Bar 3: strings 4, 5, 6 give E3, B2, E2. Beat 4 is a rest. Stop the final note and keep counting.

whole-arpeggio.title: 5. Practice the complete arpeggio
whole-arpeggio.body: Choose Practice for these three bars. There are eleven separate expected attacks, then one rest. The result evaluates audible note pitch and attack timing when supported, not whether every finger holds the Em shape.
